headline: Meta says mathematicians working with its Muse Spark chatbot have found answers to five research questions that were still open.
score_reason: Meta's own account with checks by collaborators it names; no outside peer review reported, and other teams reached some of the same answers independently.
importance_line: Working mathematicians could get a faster way to test ideas and hunt for counterexamples, but the claims come from Meta itself, no outside peer review is reported, and other teams reached some of the same answers independently.
summary: Meta says in a post on its research blog that it worked with mathematicians for several months and is sharing six papers, five of which answer questions that were still open, with its Muse Spark chatbot suggesting proofs and examples that the mathematicians then checked and corrected. Meta adds that other teams independently announced answers to some of the same problems, and says it credits them in the papers.
notes: Read the full Meta blog post; the six papers themselves were not opened. Score lowered 8 to 7 (company claim, no independent check reported).
